observations: White computerized sewing and embroidery machine.
Brand 'brother' is visible on the front left of the machine.
Model 'SE630' is printed on the top right corner of the blue floral control panel.
The machine is shown on a bed; no dedicated workspace is visible.
The LCD screen is off/dark in both photos.
A watermark 'ABIOLAONIMACHINE' and 'POSTED ON JIJI' is present across the images.
No power cord, foot pedal, embroidery hoops, or manual are visible.

claims.evidence: Requires a photo of the manufacturer's plate; Brother is a Japanese brand, but this specific model is typically manufactured in Vietnam or China.
Photos are static and do not demonstrate mechanical operation.

claims.claim: All accessories and the original manual
claims.evidence: None of the mentioned accessories or the manual are shown in the photos.
Internal condition and service history cannot be determined from external photos.

risks.risk: The computerized LCD screen or mainboard may be faulty or dead.
risks.proof: A photo or video of the machine powered on with the screen active.

risks.risk: Missing embroidery-specific accessories (hoops, embroidery foot) which are expensive to replace.
risks.proof: A photo showing the embroidery hoop and all included presser feet.
risks.if_unproven: as machine only, missing all accessories

risks.risk: Voltage mismatch; the SE630 is often a 120V North American model.
risks.proof: A photo of the power input/specification plate on the back or side.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring an external step-down transformer

risks.risk: Mechanical timing issues or needle strikes not visible when stationary.
risks.proof: A video of the machine sewing a zigzag stitch and an embroidery pattern.

proof_requests: Video of the machine powered on, navigating the menu, and sewing.
Photo of the manufacturer's label showing voltage and country of origin.
Photo of all included accessories, specifically the embroidery hoops and foot pedal.
response.reason: The model is clearly identified as a Brother SE630. It can be priced at its worst-case value (non-functional and missing accessories) until the seller provides proof of operation.
